events.summary:
Round-2 evidence resolves my two blocking concerns from round 1, and nothing new undermines H1's core chain.

(1) SCOPE — now tested and answered in the direction H1 predicts. T4/F28/F29/F32 show every measured anchor on the path steps at the same instant: exchange-gateway 0.18→~43-45% error and p99 128ms→5,170ms at ~11:01-11:02Z (F25/F26), exchange-api hop upstream 0.29→~46% error and 120ms→9,402ms (F27), order-service 0.2%→30% (F7/F10), market-data-service 0.23→6.48% (F28), api-gateway 0.26→6.15% (F29). No co-caller into exchange-gateway is healthy. The gradient descends away from the exchange-api hop (gateway upstream 45%/9.4s > gateway inbound 43%/5.2s > order-service 30%/4.3s > market-data 6.5% > api-gateway 6.2%), which is the shape of a fault at the gateway↔exchange edge, not an order-service-local one. F30 shows the one apparently-healthy signal (market-data p99 flat) is a single-metric artifact, correctly disclosed — this is exactly the discipline I asked for, and it does not weaken the scope conclusion because market-data's error_rate *is* anomalous at the same bucket.

(2) H1-vs-H4 boundary — unobservable and permanently so, now properly carried as an assumption rather than treated as resolved. F22 establishes there is no intermediate proxy/network node in the graph between exchange-gateway and the vendor, and F15/F27 confirm exchange-api is vendor-owned with has_telemetry=false. F24 shows the H4-flavoured precedent (HIST-116 envoy) scores equal to HIST-103, so precedent cannot discriminate. Both hypotheses name the same system to remediate (the gateway↔external-exchange edge); the difference between them is whether the vendor application or the path is at fault, which is a distinction for the vendor/remediation side rather than a different component to roll back here. This is a confidence cap, not a reason to hold the incident open.

Alternatives are genuinely contradicted, not merely dismissed: H2 dies on persistence past the 11:16Z rollback (F2/F14, last 504 log 12:58:54Z) plus flat order-service CPU/DB-pool (F11) and the fact that the failing 5s timeout is one layer *below* order-service (F12/F26/F27); H3 dies on the abrupt step at 11:00Z after an 88-minute quiet gap (F7) with no demand series rising (F31 flat) and a connect timeout to an external host being a reachability, not a capacity, signature (F12). F19/F20/F21 close the "unrecorded change on the failing path" alternative as far as the available tooling permits. F13/F20 confirm the change ledger holds only the two off-path changes.

What caps confidence: (a) the H1/H4 split is a naming/observation-boundary ambiguity (F12's 161 "exchange-api returned 503" entries could not be attributed to the vendor app vs. the gateway's own layer — T5.1, gap), and (b) the 240s bucket granularity cannot resolve whether the gateway's step strictly preceded order-service's, so causal ordering rests on logs (F8 11:02:45Z vs F12 11:01:25Z) rather than bucket timing. Both are real but neither changes the remediation set: the fault is at the exchange-gateway↔external-exchange hop, downstream of and below order-service. Remaining gate for full confidence is the vendor's status confirmation, which is ours to request, not to query.

I am accepting. The team should not spend the remaining budget on more of our own telemetry for this incident.

critiques.summary:
Round-2 evidence resolves my two blocking concerns from round 1, and nothing new undermines H1's core chain.

(1) SCOPE — now tested and answered in the direction H1 predicts. T4/F28/F29/F32 show every measured anchor on the path steps at the same instant: exchange-gateway 0.18→~43-45% error and p99 128ms→5,170ms at ~11:01-11:02Z (F25/F26), exchange-api hop upstream 0.29→~46% error and 120ms→9,402ms (F27), order-service 0.2%→30% (F7/F10), market-data-service 0.23→6.48% (F28), api-gateway 0.26→6.15% (F29). No co-caller into exchange-gateway is healthy. The gradient descends away from the exchange-api hop (gateway upstream 45%/9.4s > gateway inbound 43%/5.2s > order-service 30%/4.3s > market-data 6.5% > api-gateway 6.2%), which is the shape of a fault at the gateway↔exchange edge, not an order-service-local one. F30 shows the one apparently-healthy signal (market-data p99 flat) is a single-metric artifact, correctly disclosed — this is exactly the discipline I asked for, and it does not weaken the scope conclusion because market-data's error_rate *is* anomalous at the same bucket.

(2) H1-vs-H4 boundary — unobservable and permanently so, now properly carried as an assumption rather than treated as resolved. F22 establishes there is no intermediate proxy/network node in the graph between exchange-gateway and the vendor, and F15/F27 confirm exchange-api is vendor-owned with has_telemetry=false. F24 shows the H4-flavoured precedent (HIST-116 envoy) scores equal to HIST-103, so precedent cannot discriminate. Both hypotheses name the same system to remediate (the gateway↔external-exchange edge); the difference between them is whether the vendor application or the path is at fault, which is a distinction for the vendor/remediation side rather than a different component to roll back here. This is a confidence cap, not a reason to hold the incident open.

Alternatives are genuinely contradicted, not merely dismissed: H2 dies on persistence past the 11:16Z rollback (F2/F14, last 504 log 12:58:54Z) plus flat order-service CPU/DB-pool (F11) and the fact that the failing 5s timeout is one layer *below* order-service (F12/F26/F27); H3 dies on the abrupt step at 11:00Z after an 88-minute quiet gap (F7) with no demand series rising (F31 flat) and a connect timeout to an external host being a reachability, not a capacity, signature (F12). F19/F20/F21 close the "unrecorded change on the failing path" alternative as far as the available tooling permits. F13/F20 confirm the change ledger holds only the two off-path changes.

What caps confidence: (a) the H1/H4 split is a naming/observation-boundary ambiguity (F12's 161 "exchange-api returned 503" entries could not be attributed to the vendor app vs. the gateway's own layer — T5.1, gap), and (b) the 240s bucket granularity cannot resolve whether the gateway's step strictly preceded order-service's, so causal ordering rests on logs (F8 11:02:45Z vs F12 11:01:25Z) rather than bucket timing. Both are real but neither changes the remediation set: the fault is at the exchange-gateway↔external-exchange hop, downstream of and below order-service. Remaining gate for full confidence is the vendor's status confirmation, which is ours to request, not to query.

I am accepting. The team should not spend the remaining budget on more of our own telemetry for this incident.

challenges.issue: The 5s error is described as a 'connect' timeout, which is a reachability signature and does not by itself distinguish a vendor application failure (H1) from a path/DNS/egress failure (H4). The distinction survives only as an assumption because exchange-api has has_telemetry=false (F15, F22) and the 161 'exchange-api returned 503' log entries' responder could not be attributed (T5.1). This caps confidence rather than blocking the conclusion, since both readings implicate the same gateway↔external-exchange hop and the same remediation owner.

Causal ordering between exchange-gateway's step (~11:01Z) and order-service's (~11:00Z) rests on log timestamps (F12 11:01:25Z vs F8 11:02:45Z) rather than metric buckets: all key series are 240s, and F32 explicitly notes bucket granularity cannot resolve the internal ordering between 11:00Z and 11:02Z. The 'gateway first' direction is therefore inferential, not measured. This does not threaten the origin (both are on the same path) but it is the weakest measured link in the chain.

Case for 'persist past the 11:16Z rollback' relies on inference (F14) because no post-rollback order-service build/version was independently confirmed (T5.3 gap). This weakens precision of the rollback-futility claim but not H2's rejection, which independently rests on flat CPU/DB-pool (F11) and the 5s timeout being one layer below order-service (F12/F26/F27).

H4 is the only live alternative, and it is currently unfalsifiable with our telemetry: no infra/network/DNS/egress/mesh change API exists in the toolset (F19-F21 cover only deployments and config), so the absence of a recorded network change cannot be read as evidence for H1. Distinguishing connect-timeout vs response-timeout semantics from the F12 log body, and a vendor status confirmation, are the only available discriminators.
